Saving it alongside a model's training data makes a record of which checks mattered to the model, and of how that was measured. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [indent]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[2]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The number of spaces to indent nested levels by. Use `None` for the most compact output, on a single line. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The settings and results of the ablation as a JSON string. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Here's an ablation of a table of temperature readings, with three repeats. ::: {#5ba623b1 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import json import pointblank as pb import polars as pl temps = [20 + (k * 37 % 11 - 5) * 0.6 for k in range(300)] for k in range(0, 300, 25): temps[k] *= 10 readings = pl.DataFrame({"temp": temps}) def evaluate(train, *, seed, variant): sample = train.sample(fraction=1.0, with_replacement=True, seed=seed) return abs(sample["temp"].mean() - 20) validation = ( pb.Validate(data=readings) .col_vals_between(columns="temp", left=-10, right=45) .interrogate() ) ablation = ( pb.Ablation( validation, evaluate=evaluate, metric="error", higher_is_better=False, repeats=3 ) .drop_each() .run() ) print(json.dumps(json.loads(ablation.to_json())["settings"], indent=2)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` { "label": null, "metric": "error", "metrics": [ "error" ], "higher_is_better": false, "repeats": 3, "seed": 0, "control": "size_matched", "duplicates": "keep_first", "duplicates_order_by": null, "max_removed": 0.5, "conf_level": 0.95, "adjust": "holm", "ci": "t", "pass_as": "table", "evaluate_version": null, "n_rows": 300, "tbl_name": null } ``` ::: ::: The settings record everything needed to repeat the ablation with the same `evaluate()` function, including the seed.
